scenario_summary: Customer is requesting a refund for a service charge incurred 34 days ago, which is outside the standard 30-day refund window.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Emily Baker and I'm 38. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?

Hello Emily, thank you for reaching out. I understand how frustrating it can be to return from travel and find an unexpected charge. I would be happy to look into this for you. To get started, could you please provide your account email address and the last four digits of the payment method used?
Sure, my email is e.baker@email.com and the card ends in 4492.

Thank you, Emily. I have located your account. I can confirm the subscription was canceled 34 days ago. While our 'Service Terms and Refund Policy' (Section 4.2) states that refund requests must be submitted within 30 days of the transaction, I see that you have been a loyal customer with us for three years without any prior billing disputes.
That's correct, I've been with you for a long time. I really didn't use the service at all during that month since I was away.

I appreciate your loyalty, Emily. Given your account history and the fact that there was no usage recorded on the account during this billing cycle, I am authorized to make a one-time exception to our 30-day policy. I have processed a full refund of the charge to your card ending in 4492.
Oh, that is such a relief! Thank you so much for your help with this.
You are very welcome, Emily! The refund typically takes 3-5 business days to appear on your statement depending on your bank. Is there anything else I can assist you with today?

resolution_summary: The agent verified the account and service usage, then applied a one-time policy exception based on the customer's long-term loyalty and lack of service usage, successfully issuing a full refund.

judge_scores.justification: The agent handled the out-of-policy request excellently by verifying account details efficiently and demonstrating genuine empathy regarding the customer's travel situation. Furthermore, the agent correctly cited Section 4.2 of the refund policy while successfully using their authority to issue a well-justified one-time exception.
